tenuicruris:study:1.title: Tenuicruris piscanexum , a new addition to Australia’s rare Cretaceous bird fossils (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Tenuicruris is a newly described genus and species of enantiornithean bird from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Toolebuc Formation of Australia.
facts.quote: A member of Enantiornithes. The type species is T. piscanexum.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, KK F1451, is a nearly complete left tibiotarsus housed in the Kronosaurus Korner Museum.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Kronosaurus Korner Museum, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen KK F1451. It consists of a nearly complete left tibiotarsus.

facts.statement: The fossil was found about 12 km northwest of Richmond, Queensland, in the Toolebuc Formation at a public fossicking area called 'Dig Site 1'.
facts.quote: The Tenuicruris fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Toolebuc Formation about 12 km northwest of Richmond in Queensland, Australia. This site, called 'Dig Site 1', is a public fossicking area.

facts.statement: Matt A. White and colleagues formally described Tenuicruris piscanexum as a new genus and species in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Matt A. White and colleagues described Tenuicruris piscanexum as a new genus and species of enantiornithean based on these fossil remains

facts.statement: The holotype tibiotarsus measures 6.54 cm in length, about twice the length of the comparable bone in the coeval Nanantius (3.14 cm).
facts.quote: The T. piscanexum holotype tibiotarsus is 6.54 cm long. In the coeval Nanantius, this bone is about half the size, at 3.14 cm.

facts.statement: The authors noted a prominent craniolateral cnemial crest in Tenuicruris, a feature also seen in the Chinese taxa Monoenantiornis and Qiliania.
facts.quote: they also noted various similarities, such as the presence of a prominent craniolateral cnemial crest, between Tenuicruris and Monoenantiornis and Qiliania

facts.statement: Tenuicruris is the second Mesozoic bird to be formally named from Australia.
facts.quote: It is the second Mesozoic bird named from Australia.

facts.statement: It is thought that Tenuicruris inhabited the Eromanga Sea, a large inland sea that covered parts of Australia during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: se cree que habitó el mar de Eromanga, un gran mar interior.
